item.title: Missing islanders rescued after major air and sea search in Lau
item.description: Six people reported missing after their boat failed to reach its destination in the Lau Group have been rescued following a coordinated air and sea search involving the Fiji Navy, local agencies and the New Zealand Defence Force. item.content:encoded:
Six people reported missing after their boat failed to reach its destination in the Lau Group have been rescued following a coordinated air and sea search involving the Fiji Navy, local agencies and the New Zealand Defence Force.

The six had departed Namuka Island for Fulaga on the morning of August 6, but failed to arrive, prompting the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre Fiji (RCCFJ) to activate a search and rescue operation.

Search efforts involved vessels already operating in the area, while two aircraft were deployed to scour the search zone — a Northern Air Embraer EMB-110 operating as a Fiji Navy search and rescue flight and a Royal New Zealand Air Force P-8 Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft.

Together, the operation covered approximately 4,377 square nautical miles.

The Northern Air aircraft conducted a detailed search of Yagasa and nearby islands before extending its sweep across the southern section of the search area.

Meanwhile, the Royal New Zealand Air Force P-8 Poseidon completed an extensive radar search before switching to visual surveillance, successfully locating the distressed vessel at 5.30pm, just before last light.

The missing boat was found 14.6 nautical miles southwest of Vanuavatu, within the designated search area.

Following the sighting, RFNS Savenaca, which was operating nearby, was immediately diverted to the location and carried out the rescue in difficult weather conditions shortly after 8pm.

All six survivors were safely brought to Suva, where they will undergo medical assessments before being reunited with their families.

The Fiji Navy thanked all organisations and individuals who contributed to the successful operation.

item.title: Ro Teimumu hails late Tui Vuda

item.content:encoded:
ROKO Tui Drekei Ro Teimumu Kepa has paid tribute to the late Tui Vuda Ratu Eparama Kitione Tavaiqia calling the late chief a leader with good morals and high standards.

“I have received news of the passing of the Viyagwane na Jui Vuda, Ratu Eparama Kitione Tavaiqia and feel bereaved that a Paramount Chief of the Yasana o Ba and the Burebasaga Confederacy is no longer with us,” Ro Teimumu said in a statement.

“As we mourn his passing, we must hold onto the values and principles he had upheld and lived throughout his long life.

“Fiji has been blessed with chiefs like the late Turaga na Tui Vuda, who led with good morals and high standards.”

The leader of the Burebasaga confederacy extended their condolences to the family and the Vanua o Vunisei.

“I, on behalf of the Vanua o Burebasaga convey our deepest condolences to the vanua o Vunisei on the passing of a great chief whose leadership is an example to many of us that continue to lead our vanua and people.

“I, on behalf of the Matanitu Vanua o Burebasaga and my people of Rewa extend my condolences and prayers to the family of the late Turaga na Tui Vuda, the Radini Vuda and members of his household.

“Ni qai moce toka mada na Turaga na Tui Vuda.”

Traditional protocols have been observed since last Friday with the Vanua of Vuda preparing for the chiefly burial on August 12 at Viseisei village.

The late Ratu Eparama’s casket will be accorded a full military escort from the Lautoka Hospital on August 11.

item.title: Union condemns EFL over executive pay rise
item.description: The Construction Energy and Timber Workers Union of Fiji (CETWUF) has accused Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) of rewarding its senior executives with substantial salary increases while continuing to deny wage adjustments to union members. In a statement, the union National Secretary John Paul said it was “deeply concerned” by reports that the total remuneration for EFL’s Chief Executive Officer and Exec
item.content:encoded:
The Construction Energy and Timber Workers Union of Fiji (CETWUF) has accused Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) of rewarding its senior executives with substantial salary increases while continuing to deny wage adjustments to union members.

In a statement, the union National Secretary John Paul said it was “deeply concerned” by reports that the total remuneration for EFL’s Chief Executive Officer and Executive Management Group increased from $3.309 million in 2024 to $3.756 million in 2025.

The union claims its members have been denied wage increases for 2024, 2025 and now 2026 because of what it describes as EFL’s ongoing refusal to negotiate and settle the union’s log of claims.

“This glaring disparity raises serious questions about EFL’s commitment to fairness, equity, and respect for its workforce,” Paul said.

“If EFL has the financial capacity to reward its executives, it must also recognize and fairly compensate the CETWUF members whose dedication and hard work sustain EFL’s operations and success.”

The union argued that giving salary increases to one group while delaying negotiations with workers was damaging staff morale and creating unequal treatment within the organisation.

“Privileging one group while disregarding another, EFL undermines workforce morale, erodes trust, and perpetuates inequitable and discriminatory treatment,” the statement said.

CETWUF has called on EFL to immediately resume negotiations with the union to secure what it describes as a fair outcome for its members.

“CETWUF immediately calls upon EFL to engage in genuine, good-faith negotiations to secure a fair and equitable outcome for its members,” Paul said.

“Fair wages must not be reserved for a privileged few at the top but should reflect a balanced and just distribution of wage increments and improved conditions for CETWUF members.”

The union said it remained committed to maintaining constructive industrial relations but insisted there must be greater transparency and consistency in the treatment of workers.

It described the practice of granting executive pay increases while delaying the settlement of union wage claims as “unacceptable” and said it would not tolerate such actions.

CETWUF is also urging EFL’s Board and executive leadership to demonstrate fairness by entering negotiations without further delay and settling all outstanding claims lodged by the union.

item.title: Most MSMEs earn less than $500 a week – RBF survey
item.description: Small businesses continue to play an important role in supporting household incomes in Fiji, but the majority generate modest earnings and face challenges accessing finance, according to the Reserve Bank of Fiji’s 2025 Fiji Financial Services Demand Side Survey. The survey found that one in every 10 Fijian households owns a micro, small or medium enterprise (MSME), with women owning the majority o
item.content:encoded:
Small businesses continue to play an important role in supporting household incomes in Fiji, but the majority generate modest earnings and face challenges accessing finance, according to the Reserve Bank of Fiji’s 2025 Fiji Financial Services Demand Side Survey.

The survey found that one in every 10 Fijian households owns a micro, small or medium enterprise (MSME), with women owning the majority of businesses.

Of all household MSMEs, 55 per cent are owned by women, while 44 per cent are owned by men.

Most businesses operate from home, rely heavily on cash transactions and employ an average of 2.1 people.

The most common industries are food sales (48 per cent) and agriculture (24 per cent).

The survey found that 70 per cent of MSMEs earn FJ$500 or less each week, highlighting the small scale of many household businesses.

Women-owned and rural businesses generally generate lower incomes than their male-owned and urban counterparts.

Nearly 89 per cent of female-owned businesses and 92 per cent of rural MSMEs earn FJ$500 or less each week, compared with 44 per cent of male-owned and 50 per cent of urban businesses.

The report found that 75 per cent of MSMEs operate from the owner’s home, while only 19 per cent operate from towns or city locations.

The primary motivation for starting a business was to support the family, cited by 82 per cent of owners, while 38 per cent said they established their business to earn additional income.

Only 25 per cent of MSMEs had accessed a loan or grant to support their business.

Among those that secured financing, the Fiji Development Bank was the most common lender, accounting for 33 per cent of loans, followed by microfinance organisations (29 per cent). Government grants accounted for 22 per cent, while 16 per cent obtained loans from commercial banks.

Most borrowed funds were used to purchase equipment (47 per cent) or stock (40 per cent).

Despite the availability of financing, 29 per cent of MSMEs reported difficulty accessing funds.

The most common barriers included inadequate financial records or documentation (36 per cent), complex application processes (29 per cent), insufficient collateral and poor credit history.

The survey found women-owned businesses were more likely than male-owned businesses to experience difficulty obtaining finance.

Digital adoption among MSMEs remains limited.

Only 30 per cent of businesses use the internet to market or sell their products or services, although more than half of those accepting online payments do so through M-PAiSA, which accounted for 91 per cent of digital payment transactions.

The findings highlight the significant contribution of household businesses to Fiji’s economy while pointing to ongoing challenges in accessing finance, improving business capacity and expanding digital participation.

item.title: Election preparations get lift as FEO receives new fleet
item.description: THE Fiji Elections Office (FEO) is expected to reach more communities during this election period than it has in previous elections after receiving four new vehicles from the Indian High Commission to boost its operations. Speaking during an interview during the handover ceremony, Chair of the Electoral Commission Justice Usaia Ratuvili said the additional fleet would improve the Commission’s abil
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Elections Office (FEO) is expected to reach more communities during this election period than it has in previous elections after receiving four new vehicles from the Indian High Commission to boost its operations.

Speaking during an interview during the handover ceremony, Chair of the Electoral Commission Justice Usaia Ratuvili said the additional fleet would improve the Commission’s ability to carry out its work, particularly in rural areas.

Justice Ratuvili said the request for the vehicles was made during his visit to India earlier this year after the Commission identified the need for additional transport support.

He said four-wheel-drive vehicles were specifically requested because of Fiji’s terrain and the challenges faced in reaching communities where roads were not always accessible.

“We’ve just not been able to reach as wide an area as we wanted to, so with these additional vehicles for our fleet, it’s going to help us a lot,” he said.

Justice Ratuvili said the vehicles would be used across the Central, Eastern, Western and Northern divisions, assisting with voter awareness programmes, transporting election teams and moving election equipment, including ballot boxes.

He also confirmed that Fiji had requested indelible ink from India for the upcoming elections.

Indian High Commissioner to Fiji Shri Suneet Mehta said the donation was another milestone in the longstanding relationship between India and Fiji.

“India has provided not only the vehicles but also indelible ink for various general elections,” he said.

Mr Mehta said the latest assistance demonstrated India’s continued support for the conduct of free, transparent and inclusive elections in Fiji.

item.title: El Niño warning: ‘Prepare now, don’t panic’
item.description: FIJI should prepare for a prolonged period of dry weather rather than panic, as the Fiji Meteorological Service confirms a strong El Niño is already underway and is expected to continue into next year. Acting director of the Fiji Meteorological Service Samisoni Waqavakatoga said forecasts indicated the climate pattern would persist through 2026 and into 2027, although its full impacts remained unc
item.content:encoded:
FIJI should prepare for a prolonged period of dry weather rather than panic, as the Fiji Meteorological Service confirms a strong El Niño is already underway and is expected to continue into next year.

Acting director of the Fiji Meteorological Service Samisoni Waqavakatoga said forecasts indicated the climate pattern would persist through 2026 and into 2027, although its full impacts remained uncertain.

“Fiji should be prepared rather than panic,” he said.

“The Fiji Meteorological Service confirms that El Niño is underway. El Niño is underway and most models project this El Niño status to last through 2026 and into 2027.”

He said while the severity of the event could not yet be confirmed, drier-than-normal conditions were already being experienced.

“We cannot yet confirm how severe this El Niño event will be.”

Mr Waqavakatoga said people should take practical steps now to prepare for the coming months.

“The advice from the Fiji Met Service for the general public is prepare now, store water, secure your homes and protect food sources before the dry spell kicks in.”

He stressed that preparation, rather than fear, was the most important response.

REDUCED rainfall forecast under a very strong El Niño is expected to place Fiji’s agriculture sector under increasing pressure in the months ahead.

The warning comes as farmers are encouraged to begin adapting their planting practices before dry conditions worsen.

Agriculture is expected to be among the hardest-hit sectors, Fiji Meteorological Service acting director Samisoni Waqavakatoga said in an interview on The Fiji Times online portal, The Lens@177.

“With the agricultural sector, the impacts will be mostly felt by them,” he said.

He said prolonged dry weather would directly affect crop production.

“With these dry conditions, we could see less rainfall in the coming months.

“So definitely with less rainfall, the agricultural sector, with crops and crop production, will be most affected.”

Mr Waqavakatoga said farmers should begin preparing now.

“One of the ways farmers should prepare for this prolonged dry spell is to adopt climate-smart practices, planting practices that conserve soil moisture and look into diversifying crop choices to suit the dry conditions that we are expecting.”

FIJI Meteorological Service acting director Samisoni Waqavakatoga has urged families across the country to store fresh water now as strong El Niño is expected to cause extreme dry conditions in the coming months.

Speaking during an interview on The Fiji Times online portal, The Lens@177, Mr Waqavakatoga said water conservation and storage should become part of every household’s preparations before the dry spell intensifies.

Instead, he said preparation was the key message Fiji Met wanted communities to take on board.

“Preparation is vital – storing water is important.”

Mr Waqavakatoga said Fiji Met’s seasonal outlooks had consistently highlighted the likelihood of El Niño continuing into next year.

“The advisories have included the El Niño forecast that it will persist for the next coming months into next year.”

He encouraged households to use water wisely.

“For the general public, it’s just to use water wisely – the main thing is to store water for the coming months, especially for the homes.

“That’s to cater for the dry months coming up.”

AGRICULTURE, tourism and fisheries are among the sectors expected to face major challenges as Fiji enters a prolonged period of dry conditions linked to a very strong El Niño.

Speaking during an interview with The Fiji Times online portal, The Lens@177, acting director Fiji Meteorological Service Samisoni Waqavakatoga said the impact would be felt across key sectors, with agriculture expected to be among the hardest hit.

“The sectors that will be most vulnerable are the agriculture, the tourism and fisheries – also with the energy utilities,” he said.

item.title: Couple’s Australia reunion dream ends in tragedy
item.description: A journey filled with anticipation and love turned into unimaginable heartbreak on Wednesday when an elderly couple travelling to reunite with their children in Australia lost their lives in a horrific four-vehicle crash at Vakabalea, Navua. A family member said Kaminieli Matadradra, 70, and his wife Setaita, 67, were due to board a flight from Nadi today, carrying with them the excitement of seei
item.content:encoded:
A journey filled with anticipation and love turned into unimaginable heartbreak on Wednesday when an elderly couple travelling to reunite with their children in Australia lost their lives in a horrific four-vehicle crash at Vakabalea, Navua.

A family member said Kaminieli Matadradra, 70, and his wife Setaita, 67, were due to board a flight from Nadi today, carrying with them the excitement of seeing family they had longed to embrace. Instead, their loved ones are now preparing for a funeral instead of a joyful reunion.

Police said the vehicle carrying the couple crossed into the opposite lane, triggering a collision involving four vehicles.

The National Fire Authority (NFA) said emergency crews responded within minutes but found the couple had died at the scene. Two other people, including a pregnant woman, were injured and taken to the Navua Hospital.

As grief ripples through two families and across communities, NFA’s chief executive officer Puamau Sowane pleaded with motorists to make safety their priority.

“No journey is worth risking a life,” he said, urging drivers to slow down, remain alert and exercise patience on the roads. The tragedy has pushed Fiji’s road death toll to 31 this year, a painful reminder that in an instant, a long-awaited family reunion can become a lifetime of loss.

item.title: Queens set for festival reunion
item.description: FORMER Hibiscus queens from as far back as 1956 will return to the spotlight this month as the festival celebrates seven decades of history at Albert Park, Suva. Festival organisers have confirmed that queens from different eras of the festival will make special appearances, bringing together a legacy that began with the inaugural event in 1956.
item.content:encoded:
FORMER Hibiscus queens from as far back as 1956 will return to the spotlight this month as the festival celebrates seven decades of history at Albert Park, Suva.

Festival organisers have confirmed that queens from different eras of the festival will make special appearances, bringing together a legacy that began with the inaugural event in 1956.

Director Ellen Whippy-Knight said the reunion was part of efforts to revive the glamour and significance of the festival while celebrating the women who had carried its legacy over the years.

“I am now absolutely delighted to confirm we will have personal appearances from these former queens,” she said.

The former queens expected to attend include the first Hibiscus Queen, Liebling Hoeflich from 1956, along with winners from different decades including Eta Ulavula, Michele Smith, Annie Reymond, Lenora Qereqeretabua, Lynda Tabuya, Patricia Naisara, Merewalesi Nailatikau, Alisi Rabukawaqa, Melania Tora and outgoing queen Rhyelle Aisea.

Ms Whippy-Knight said the highlight would be the appearance of the top three contestants from the first Hibiscus Queen pageant, including winner Liebling Hoeflich and runners-up Susan Curtis and Lydia Pickering.

She said former queens would also play a role as mentors and role models for current contestants, sharing their experiences and stories.

“It’s wonderful that contestants can see real role models who have won the crown.”

The 70th FMF Hibiscus Festival will be held at Albert Park from August 29 to September 5.
